newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand comfortable with Q4 forecasts.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand comfortable with Q4 forecasts.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc president Alex Yemenidjian on Wednesday said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus estimate that the company would post earnings of $0.39 a share for the fourth quarter.
In an interview with Reuters, Yemenidjian said the holiday season at the Las Vegas MGM Grand had been "one of the strongest" he could remember.
He said the high-end business, which includes gambling at baccarat tables, was about normal but the overall volume of players was higher than usual.
At the company's casino at Darwin, Australia, he said MGM "played lucky in its high-end business."
The company's 50 percent-owned New York, New York Hotel in Las Vegas opened to very strong business with management having to close the casinos doors periodically for crowd control, Yemenidjian said.
The hotel is running at 100 percent occupancy with 75 percent devoted to the more lucrative independent traveler sector and about 25 percent devoted to tour and travel guests.
New York, New York, which is also 50 percent-owned by Primadonna Resorts, opened on January 3.
When the MGM Grand Hotel opened in 1993, the hotel devoted 45 percent of its rooms to the tour and travel business, which contributed to lower-than-expected yield.
But at New York, New York, that has not been the case, he said. "Every single day has exceeded our expectations," Yemenidjian said.
While he declined to comment on exact figures of casino revenue, he said both slot machine play and table game play had exceeded company expectations.
MGM Grand reported earnings of $0.66 a share in the fourth quarter of 1995.

Montgomery Securities David McDonald analyst said the wide differential between EPS in the 1995 quarter and the 1996 period reflected tax-loss carryforwards that enabled MGM to avoid tax payments last year.
"On a normalized tax basis, last year's fourth quarter earnings would have been about $0.42 a share," McDonald said.
